r: léi shēng dà, yǔ diǎn xiǎo
mean: much fanfare at the start, little real action after
lit: loud thunder, tiny raindrops: a storm that roars but hardly rains

use.how: Usually a predicate, often after 又是/总是: 这次整改又是雷声大，雨点小。 Criticises plans, campaigns or threats announced loudly that deliver little.

near.diff: 虎头蛇尾 is starting strong and fizzling out as the work goes on; 雷声大，雨点小 stresses loud announcements or threats followed by little real action.

cue: The company launched a 'green office' drive with posters, slogans and a big kick-off meeting; three months later nothing at all had changed.

ctx.s: 他天天说要减肥，结果还是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: He talks about losing weight every day, but it's all talk and very little action.

ctx.s: 妈妈每次都说要没收我的手机，可每次都{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: Mum always says she'll confiscate my phone, but it's always a lot of noise and nothing happens.

ctx.s: 公司宣传了半天的新福利，最后只发了一张购物卡，真是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: The company hyped its new staff benefits for ages, and in the end all we got was one shopping card. So much fanfare for so little.

ctx.s: “上次你说要整顿纪律，怎么又是{雷声大，雨点小}？”同事笑着问经理。
ctx.en: "Last time you said you'd tighten discipline. How come it was all noise again?" a colleague asked the manager with a laugh.

ctx.s: 小区说要彻底清理楼道里的杂物，大家都担心又是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: The estate announced it would clear all the clutter out of the stairwells, and everyone worried it would be big talk and little action again.

ctx.s: 开会时人人都说要合作，真到出钱出力的时候却{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: At the meeting everyone talked about working together, but when it came to putting in money and effort, there was little to show for it.

bad.s: 昨天的音乐会{雷声大，雨点小}，观众都特别满意。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday's concert was loud and lively and the audience loved it)
bad.why: It is a criticism of big announcements followed by little action, never praise for a loud or exciting event.

bad.s: 他说话声音很大，做事却很细心，是个{雷声大，雨点小}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he has a loud voice but works carefully)
bad.why: It does not describe a loud voice; it criticises big talk, plans or threats that lead to little real action.

mean: the truth can't be covered up for long; it will come out
lit: paper cannot wrap up fire: sooner or later the flame burns through

use.how: A whole clause, often a warning: 纸包不住火，你还是说实话吧。 Said about lies, cover-ups and hidden wrongdoing that will come to light.

near.diff: 此地无银三百两 is a clumsy denial that itself gives the secret away; 纸包不住火 says any concealed fact will come out in time.

cue: A friend has hidden a failed exam from their parents for weeks and plans to keep lying. You warn them it will come out anyway.

ctx.s: 你别再瞒着了，{纸包不住火}，老师迟早会知道的。
ctx.en: Stop hiding it. You can't keep something like this covered up; the teacher will find out sooner or later.

ctx.s: “这件事能瞒多久？”“{纸包不住火}，早点说出来反而好。”
ctx.en: "How long can we keep this quiet?" "Not long; the truth always comes out. It's better to say it early."

ctx.s: 她把车撞坏了却不敢告诉丈夫，可心里清楚{纸包不住火}。
ctx.en: She dented the car and didn't dare tell her husband, but she knew perfectly well he would find out.

ctx.s: 产品有问题就该马上召回，{纸包不住火}，拖下去公司的名声就完了。
ctx.en: If a product is faulty it should be recalled at once. It will come out anyway, and if you stall, the company's reputation is finished.

ctx.s: 他偷偷挪用公款，以为没人发现，可{纸包不住火}，半年后还是被查出来了。
ctx.en: He secretly took company money and thought no one would notice, but it couldn't stay hidden: six months later he was found out.

ctx.s: 那家餐厅用过期食材的事，终究是{纸包不住火}，被一名员工曝光了。
ctx.en: In the end the restaurant couldn't hide its use of expired ingredients; one of its own staff exposed it.

bad.s: 他升职的好消息{纸包不住火}，大家很快就都知道了。
bad.en: (meant: the good news of his promotion spread quickly)
bad.why: It is about a secret or wrongdoing someone tries to hide coming out, not about good news spreading.

bad.s: 她脾气很急，就像{纸包不住火}，一点小事就发火。
bad.en: (meant: she has a hot temper and flares up over little things)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with temper or feelings bursting out; it says a concealed fact cannot stay hidden.

t: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门
r: bù zuò kuī xīn shì, bù pà guǐ qiāo mén
mean: with a clear conscience you have nothing to fear
lit: do nothing that weighs on your conscience, and you need not fear a ghost knocking at your door

use.how: A whole clause, said by someone suspected or investigated to show they are calm and innocent, or as moral advice: 查就查吧，不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门。

near.diff: 真金不怕火炼 is about real quality surviving a test; 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门 is about having done nothing wrong and so fearing no investigation.

cue: Auditors arrive and the whole office is nervous, but the accountant calmly opens every book: she has never fiddled a single figure.

ctx.s: 查就查吧，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: Let them check. I've done nothing wrong, so I've nothing to be afraid of.

ctx.s: 有人说他收了回扣，他笑着说：“{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}，随便查。”
ctx.en: Someone claimed he had taken kickbacks. He just smiled: "My conscience is clear. Check whatever you like."

ctx.s: 你要是真没拿那笔钱，怕什么？{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: If you really didn't take the money, what are you afraid of? If you've done nothing wrong, you've nothing to fear.

ctx.s: 警察上门了解情况，老张一点也不慌，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}嘛。
ctx.en: When the police came round asking questions, Lao Zhang wasn't flustered at all. He had nothing on his conscience, after all.

ctx.s: 奶奶常教育我们做人要老实，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: Grandma always taught us to be honest: if you do nothing to be ashamed of, you never have to be afraid.

ctx.s: 公司要公开各部门的账目，别人都紧张，财务主管却很坦然：{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: The company was going to open every department's accounts. Others were nervous, but the finance manager was calm: with a clean record, there was nothing to fear.

bad.s: 他胆子很大，晚上一个人走山路，真是{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
bad.en: (meant: he's brave enough to walk a mountain path alone at night)
bad.why: It is about a clear conscience when facing suspicion, not physical courage or not being scared of the dark.

bad.s: 这次考试我准备得很充分，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
bad.en: (meant: I've prepared well, so I'm not worried about the exam)
bad.why: It means being innocent of wrongdoing; being well prepared for a test has nothing to do with conscience.

r: zhēn jīn bù pà huǒ liàn
mean: what is genuine holds up under any test
lit: real gold does not fear the smelting fire: the heat only proves it is pure

use.how: A whole clause, said when something is doubted or put to a test: 真金不怕火炼，欢迎检测。 Used of products, skill, character or relationships confident of passing scrutiny.

near.diff: 是金子总会发光 says real talent will be noticed sooner or later; 真金不怕火炼 says what is genuine will survive doubt and testing.

cue: A rival claims a small farm's honey is fake. The owner cheerfully sends samples to three independent labs, sure of the results.

ctx.s: 我们的产品质量没问题，{真金不怕火炼}，欢迎检测。
ctx.en: There's nothing wrong with our products. The genuine article can stand any test, so feel free to have them checked.

ctx.s: 这块玉是不是真的，拿去鉴定一下就知道了，{真金不怕火炼}嘛。
ctx.en: Whether this jade is real, a valuation will tell us. If it's genuine, it'll pass.

ctx.s: 有人怀疑他的数据是编的，他只说：“{真金不怕火炼}，你们尽管重做实验。”
ctx.en: Some suspected his data was made up. He simply said: "Real results stand up to anything. Go ahead and repeat the experiment."

ctx.s: 两人的感情经历了异地和失业，{真金不怕火炼}，反而更深了。
ctx.en: Their relationship went through living apart and losing jobs, and like true gold in the fire, it only grew deeper.

ctx.s: 这位选手的实力经过一场场大赛的考验，证明了{真金不怕火炼}。
ctx.en: This player's ability has been tested in one major tournament after another, proving that true quality holds up under pressure.

ctx.s: 面对一轮又一轮的质疑，这位老教授只说了一句：{真金不怕火炼}。
ctx.en: Faced with round after round of doubts, the old professor said only one thing: what is genuine fears no test.

bad.s: 这口锅是铸铁的，{真金不怕火炼}，可以直接放在火上烧。
bad.en: (meant: this pan is cast iron, so it can go straight on the flame)
bad.why: It is figurative, about something genuine passing a test or scrutiny, not about objects that can stand heat.

bad.s: 他刚进公司没多久就被老板看中了，真是{真金不怕火炼}。
bad.en: (meant: his talent was spotted soon after he joined)
bad.why: Being noticed quickly is a different saying; this one needs a doubt or a test that something genuine survives.

r: yī rén zuò shì yī rén dāng
mean: I alone take the consequences of what I did
lit: one person did the deed, so that one person bears it

use.how: A whole clause, usually said by the one responsible to stop others sharing the blame: 是我弄的，一人做事一人当。 Also used as advice to take responsibility.

near.diff: 敢作敢当 describes a person's character as bold and responsible; 一人做事一人当 is said at the moment of owning one specific act.

cue: The whole class is going to be kept in for a broken window. One boy stands up, says he did it alone, and asks that the others go home.

ctx.s: 窗户是我打破的，{一人做事一人当}，别怪他们。
ctx.en: I broke the window. It's on me alone, so don't blame them.

ctx.s: “要不我跟老师说是我干的吧。”“不用，{一人做事一人当}，我自己去说。”
ctx.en: "Shall I tell the teacher it was me?" "No need. I did it, I'll face it. I'll go and tell him myself."

ctx.s: 你已经是大人了，要学会{一人做事一人当}，别总让父母替你收拾。
ctx.en: You're an adult now. You need to learn to own what you do and stop having your parents clean up after you.

ctx.s: 他刮了别人的车，没有开走，而是留了张纸条：“是我刮的，{一人做事一人当}。”
ctx.en: He scraped someone's car and didn't drive off; he left a note: "I scraped it, and I'll take responsibility."

ctx.s: 方案出了错，他主动向老板承认，说{一人做事一人当}，不能让组员背锅。
ctx.en: When the plan went wrong he went to the boss himself, saying the blame was his alone and his team shouldn't carry it.

ctx.s: 武侠小说里的英雄常把{一人做事一人当}挂在嘴边，从不连累朋友。
ctx.en: Heroes in martial-arts novels are always saying they alone will answer for their deeds, and they never drag their friends into trouble.

bad.s: 这个项目太大，我们不能{一人做事一人当}，得分工合作。
bad.en: (meant: the project is too big for one person; we must divide the work)
bad.why: It is about taking the blame for one's own act, not about one person doing all the work.

bad.s: 老板对员工说：“这次成功，{一人做事一人当}，功劳全是你的。”
bad.en: (meant: this success is all your credit)
bad.why: It is about bearing the consequences of a mistake or misdeed, not about who gets the credit for a success.

r: wú shì bù dēng sān bǎo diàn
mean: I only come calling when there is a favour to ask
lit: with no business, one does not climb up to the hall of the Three Jewels

story.text: The Three Jewels (san bao) is the Buddhist name for the Buddha, his teaching (the Dharma) and the community of monks (the Sangha). A 'hall of the Three Jewels' is the hall of a Buddhist temple where they are honoured: a solemn place that people did not wander into idly but visited for a purpose, to pray or ask for help. The saying borrows this to admit, half jokingly, that a visit has a request behind it.
story.source: Buddhist term 三宝 (the Three Jewels)

use.how: A whole clause, said by a visitor of themselves (我今天是无事不登三宝殿) or teasingly by the host (你是无事不登三宝殿吧). Admits a visit comes with a favour to ask.

near.diff: 临时抱佛脚 is scrambling to prepare at the last minute; 无事不登三宝殿 is visiting someone only because you need something from them.

cue: An old classmate you haven't heard from in a year turns up with a bag of fruit, smiles, and admits there's a little something he needs your help with.

ctx.s: 老同学笑着说：“我今天是{无事不登三宝殿}，想请你帮个忙。”
ctx.en: My old classmate said with a smile: "I'll be honest, I haven't come just to chat. I'd like to ask you a favour."

ctx.s: 你平时很少来我这儿，今天是{无事不登三宝殿}吧？说吧，什么事？
ctx.en: You hardly ever drop by, so you must want something today. Go on, what is it?

ctx.s: 邻居提着水果来敲门，我心里明白，他{无事不登三宝殿}。
ctx.en: When my neighbour knocked on the door holding a bag of fruit, I knew he hadn't come for nothing.

ctx.s: 小李一进门就帮经理倒茶，经理笑了：“{无事不登三宝殿}，有话直说吧。”
ctx.en: Xiao Li came in and poured the manager a cup of tea straight away. The manager laughed: "You don't come here without a reason. Out with it."

ctx.s: 这么晚打扰您真不好意思，我也是{无事不登三宝殿}，孩子上学的事想请您指点一下。
ctx.en: Sorry to bother you so late. I wouldn't come without a reason: I'd like your advice about my child's schooling.

ctx.s: 表弟一年没联系，突然请我吃饭，果然是{无事不登三宝殿}，想借我的车。
ctx.en: My cousin hadn't been in touch for a year and suddenly invited me to dinner. Sure enough, he wanted something: to borrow my car.

bad.s: 我奶奶信佛，每个星期都去寺庙，真是{无事不登三宝殿}。
bad.en: (meant: my grandmother is Buddhist and goes to the temple every week)
bad.why: It is not about going to temples; it jokes that someone pays a visit only because they want a favour.

bad.s: 你有空常来玩，我们家{无事不登三宝殿}，随时欢迎！
bad.en: (meant: come round whenever you like, you're always welcome)
bad.why: It says people visit only when they need something, so it cannot serve as a warm open invitation.

r: yuǎn shuǐ jiě bu liǎo jìn kě
mean: help that is far away is no use for an urgent need
lit: far-off water cannot quench a thirst that is close at hand

story.text: Duke Mu of Lu sent his sons to serve at the courts of the powerful states of Jin and Jing (Chu), hoping for their protection. One of his advisers objected: if a child is drowning and you send all the way to Yue for a swimmer, however good, the child will die; if a fire breaks out and you fetch water from the sea, the fire will not go out. Far water does not save you from a near fire. Jin and Jing are strong, but Qi is right next door. The modern saying puts thirst in place of the fire.
story.source: 《韩非子·说林上》 (as 远水不救近火)

use.how: A whole clause, often after 可是/但是: 他答应下个月寄钱，可远水解不了近渴。 Said when help that is promised or distant cannot meet a pressing need.

near.diff: 远亲不如近邻 says neighbours help more than distant relatives; 远水解不了近渴 says any help that is too far off or too late is useless right now.

cue: Your rent is due tomorrow, and the bank says the money your parents sent from abroad will take two weeks to arrive.

ctx.s: 我急着用钱，可父母都在外地，就算想帮忙也是{远水解不了近渴}。
ctx.en: I need money urgently, but my parents live in another city; even if they want to help, they're too far away to do anything now.

ctx.s: 他说下个月发了工资就还我，可我明天就要交房租，{远水解不了近渴}啊。
ctx.en: He says he'll pay me back when he gets paid next month, but my rent is due tomorrow. That's no help now.

ctx.s: “补贴明年才发下来。”“{远水解不了近渴}，店这个月就撑不住了。”
ctx.en: "The subsidy won't be paid until next year." "That's too late to help; the shop won't make it through this month."

ctx.s: 新招的人下个月才到岗，{远水解不了近渴}，这周的活只能我们加班干。
ctx.en: The new hires don't start until next month, which doesn't help us now; we'll have to do overtime to get this week's work done.

ctx.s: 等总部派人来修要三天，{远水解不了近渴}，咱们能不能先找本地的师傅？
ctx.en: Waiting for headquarters to send someone will take three days, and we can't wait that long. Can we find a local repairman first?

ctx.s: 暴雨冲断了公路，救援物资还在几十公里外，{远水解不了近渴}，村民们只好互相帮助。
ctx.en: The storm washed out the road and the relief supplies were still dozens of kilometres away, too far to help, so the villagers had to rely on each other.

bad.s: 我渴极了，可是{远水解不了近渴}，就去买了一瓶水。
bad.en: (meant: I was really thirsty, so I bought a bottle of water)
bad.why: It is figurative, about distant or late help for an urgent problem, not about actually being thirsty.

bad.s: 他住得离我很远，我们{远水解不了近渴}，很少见面。
bad.en: (meant: he lives far from me, so we rarely meet)
bad.why: It is not about friends living far apart; it says help that arrives from afar or too late can't meet an urgent need.

r: wū lòu piān féng lián yè yǔ
mean: misfortune piles on when you are already in trouble
lit: the roof is leaking, and just then it rains night after night

use.how: A whole clause, a sigh over bad luck, usually with both blows named: 真是屋漏偏逢连夜雨，刚丢了工作又生了病。

near.diff: 雪上加霜 is a four-character comment that something made a bad situation worse; 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 is a full, sighing saying about bad luck hitting when you're already down.

cue: The day after a man loses his job, his car breaks down and his landlord announces a rent rise.

ctx.s: 我刚丢了钱包，手机又摔坏了，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
ctx.en: I'd just lost my wallet, and then I broke my phone too. When it rains, it pours.

ctx.s: “你脸色怎么这么差？”“别提了，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}，感冒还没好又扭了脚。”
ctx.en: "Why do you look so awful?" "Don't ask. One thing after another: I'm not over my cold yet and now I've twisted my ankle."

ctx.s: 赶飞机已经晚了，路上偏偏又堵车，这不是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}吗？
ctx.en: I was already late for my flight, and then I got stuck in traffic. Isn't that just bad luck piling on?

ctx.s: 公司本来就在亏钱，最大的客户又走了，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}啊。
ctx.en: The company was already losing money, and now its biggest client has left. Trouble on top of trouble.

ctx.s: 那年家里的小店刚倒闭，父亲又住了院，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}，日子特别难。
ctx.en: That year our family's little shop had just closed down when Dad was taken into hospital. Misfortune kept piling on, and life was very hard.

ctx.s: 球队本就有两名主力受伤，赛前一晚队长又发起高烧，可谓{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
ctx.en: The team already had two key players injured, and on the eve of the match the captain came down with a high fever: one blow after another.

bad.s: 我考上了大学，又中了奖，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
bad.en: (meant: I got into university and won a prize, two pieces of good luck)
bad.why: It is only for misfortune piling up; two pieces of good news at once calls for a different saying.

bad.s: 我的手机屏幕裂了，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
bad.en: (meant: my phone screen cracked, what bad luck)
bad.why: One mishap alone does not fit; it needs a fresh blow landing on top of trouble that was already there.

t: 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧
r: liú de qīng shān zài, bù pà méi chái shāo
mean: as long as the essentials survive, there is hope to recover
lit: keep the green hills standing, and you'll never run short of firewood to burn

use.how: A whole clause of advice or comfort after a loss or before a sacrifice: 钱没了可以再挣，留得青山在，不怕没柴烧。 Says protect what matters most, rebuild later.

near.diff: 车到山前必有路 says a way out will turn up by itself; 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧 says to protect what matters most, such as health, so you can recover.

cue: A friend's restaurant has failed and he wants to keep working while ill to pay off debts. You tell him to get his health back first; he can always start again.

ctx.s: 生意没了可以再做，身体最要紧，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
ctx.en: You can always start another business; your health is what matters most. As long as you're well, you can rebuild.

ctx.s: 你现在硬撑下去，万一累倒了怎么办？{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}啊。
ctx.en: If you push on like this and collapse, what then? Keep yourself in one piece and there will be other chances.

ctx.s: 公司决定卖掉两家分店，保住总店，老板说：“{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。”
ctx.en: The company decided to sell two branches to save the main store. The boss said: "As long as the core survives, we can grow again."

ctx.s: 一场大火烧了仓库，好在没人受伤，爷爷说{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
ctx.en: A fire destroyed the warehouse, but luckily no one was hurt. Grandpa said that as long as we're all alive and well, we can build everything up again.

ctx.s: 别为了一次升职把身体熬垮了，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}嘛。
ctx.en: Don't wear yourself out for one promotion. Stay healthy and there'll be plenty more opportunities.

ctx.s: 球队虽然输了决赛，但核心队员都还在，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}，明年再来。
ctx.en: The team lost the final, but its core players are all staying. With the essentials intact, they can come back and try again next year.

bad.s: 我们去山里砍柴吧，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
bad.en: (meant: let's go and collect firewood in the hills)
bad.why: It is figurative comfort or advice about loss and recovery, not a remark about hills or firewood.

bad.s: 他已经很有钱了，还在拼命赚钱，真是{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
bad.en: (meant: he's already rich and still works himself hard for money)
bad.why: It is said after a setback to save the essentials for later, not to describe someone greedy or hard-working.

r: sǐ mǎ dàng huó mǎ yī
mean: to try anything anyway, though the case looks hopeless
lit: to treat a dead horse as though it were still alive

use.how: Usually a predicate, often with 只好/就 or ending in 吧: 只好死马当活马医了。 Said, with a wry shrug, of trying a last unlikely fix because nothing else is left.

near.diff: 病急乱投医 criticises grabbing at any help in a panic; 死马当活马医 is a knowing last try, made while expecting little.

cue: Two repair shops say your old laptop is beyond saving, but before throwing it out you try a random fix you saw in a video anyway.
